summary.intent: Continue orchestrating the GSD phase 70.1 workflow — after research and planning produced 13 PLAN.md files across 7 waves (covering TS/Rust rotation-engine soundness fixes and desktop FUSE RotationDeps live-wiring), execute all plans using wave-based parallel execution with independent git worktrees for concurrent plans.
summary.outcome: Successfully merged Waves 1-4 (10/13 plans) using parallel git worktrees, discovered and fixed a genuine product bug (decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering flaw in both TS and Rust rotation engines) surfaced by the new depth-3 anti-vacuous e2e fixture, then completed Waves 5-6 (plans 11-12) sequentially on the main branch; only Wave 7 (plan 13, the human-gated desktop-e2e checkpoint) remains.

repo: Decision-coverage gate parser (.claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/decisions.cjs) only accepts three D-NN bullet forms: '- **D-NN:** text', '- **D-NN — title** body', or '- **D-NN: Title.** body' — a single malformed bullet (e.g. period before closing '**') causes it to bail on ALL decisions (0/N), not just the malformed one.
execute-phase worktree auto-degrade (#683) drops to sequential execution if HEAD diverged from the worktree fork base, unless worktree.baseRef is explicitly set to 'head'.

Executors running unscoped `cargo fmt --all` (instead of `cargo fmt -p <crate>`) leave workspace-wide out-of-scope formatting drift uncommitted in the worktree, which blocks cleanup-wave's merge with worktree_dirty; must diff-verify it's formatting-only before discarding.

packages/sdk-core unit tests mocked `unsealChildReadKey` to unconditionally succeed regardless of key, which masked a real AEAD key-mismatch bug (decrypt attempted before dirtiness check) for the entire life of the rotation engine feature — real-crypto e2e fixtures were the first thing to catch it.

tests/sdk-e2e/vitest config has no dotenv loader and the test script is bare `vitest run` — .env must be sourced into the shell manually or auth (test-login) 401s with a misleading 'Invalid test login secret' error even when secrets match.

packages/sdk consumer tests run against the built dist, not source — after changing packages/sdk-core mid-phase, forgetting to rebuild sdk-core+sdk dists causes spurious cross-package test failures that look like regressions but are dist staleness.

crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs independently duplicates the FUSE gate-ordering pattern and cannot be cargo-checked on macOS (winfsp-sys needs Windows COM APIs) — fixes to the Unix path don't propagate there; it's a WinFsp-parity follow-up.
gsd_run loop render-hooks plan:pre --raw emits invalid JSON (literal newlines in fragments); read the underlying hooks JSON file directly with Read instead.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier unconditionally AEAD-decrypted a child's sealed ref via resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope before checking childPub.generation > childRef.generation; for a genuinely dirty edge where the parent also rotated, decryption with the current key must throw. Fixed by fetching childPub via resolveAndFetchNode first, comparing generations, and only decrypting confirmed-clean edges; dirty items now carry nodeReadKey: undefined and route through repairDirtyNode (ECIES checkpoint) or fail closed with DirtyNodeUnrecoverableError.

resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope bundled 'fetch child's public envelope' and 'decrypt the child's key' into one call, preventing the dirtiness check from running before decrypt; factored out unsealChildReadKeyFromPub to separate fetch from decrypt.

verify_subtree_clean was non-recursive and treated a missing root node as clean (empty frontier indistinguishable from converged); fixed via new VerifySubtreeOutcome{is_dirty,frontier} shape and explicit-work-stack recursion (collect_dirty_frontier helper).
rotate_read_on_scope_exit stub returned Err (fail-closed EIO) — documented as a deliberately deferred 'LIVE-WIRING RESIDUAL'; later wired to production FuseRotationDeps adapter in plan 09.

New production RotationDeps adapter (FuseRotationDeps/ApiClientTransport) built in plan 09; IPNS signing-key sourced from local InodeTable with fail-closed behavior for non-materialized nodes — a gap RESEARCH didn't specify a source for.

unlink_shared_scope_exit_fails_closed_until_rotation_wired test needed inversion (assert success) but production run_scope_exit_gate hardcodes ApiClientTransport; plan 12 built an in-process std::net::TcpListener mock IPNS HTTP server with a real Ed25519 keypair to exercise the actual production transport path rather than fake a pass.

workflow: When a background subagent's returned worktree metadata JSON has a mislabeled field (e.g. expected_base showing its own final commit instead of the true fork base), verify the actual fork base independently via the branch-check guard rather than trusting the label.

For cross-plan integration risk (e.g. two plans touching the same function signature from different bases), run a synchronous cross-plan compile/test check on the merged tree immediately after merging, rather than waiting for the full post-merge gate.
When a post-merge gate fails unexpectedly right after a wave where an earlier wave changed a dependency package, suspect stale build dist before suspecting a real regression — rebuild dists first.

On core-gate failures (e.g. e2e crash-safety), dispatch a dedicated diagnostic subagent instructed to distinguish 'fixture bug' from 'product bug' via scientific method with reverted instrumentation, rather than letting the same executor patch tests to pass.
Independently re-verify a subagent's 'all green' claim on a core/critical gate (rebuild + re-run yourself) before marking a wave/task complete, even after a detailed fix report.
Commit-tool timeouts on large files (e.g. ROADMAP.md lint-staged hook) should be checked via git log rather than retried — false negatives are common per prior memory.
When running multiple worktree-isolated agents, dispatch git worktree add calls one message at a time to avoid .git/config.lock races; once created, execution proceeds fully in parallel.

friction: Confusion at Wave 1 start: user challenged why only 1 of 4 plans was executing — orchestrator had silently decided to run a synchronous 'canary' plan first without flagging that intent, causing a false impression of sequential-only execution.
decision-coverage gate blocking failure was a pure parse-format issue (D-09/D-10 bullet punctuation) unrelated to actual coverage, costing several diagnostic steps to trace to the parser regex.
state.planned-phase and ROADMAP annotate tools silently no-op'd ('updated: []'/'updated: false') on this STATE.md/ROADMAP.md format, requiring manual edits as a workaround.
cleanup-wave merge blocked on Wave 1 plan 03 due to unscoped `cargo fmt --all` leaving 13 unrelated files dirty in the worktree — required manual diff verification before discarding.
sdk-e2e test-login 401 with matching secrets was misleading; root cause (no dotenv loader in vitest config, .env not exported to shell) took several steps to isolate.
Post-merge gate for Wave 3 showed 3 spurious test failures due to stale sdk-core dist not rebuilt after Wave 2's engine.ts changes — looked like a regression at first.

Depth-3 e2e crash-resume fixtures (plan 10) surfaced a genuine, previously undetected product bug (decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering) that blocked Wave 4 completion and required a full diagnose-then-fix subagent cycle across both TS and Rust engines.

Stale/false rust-analyzer diagnostic (macros.rs:50 AncestorChain type mismatch) caused a moment of concern after plan 11, requiring manual verification that the authoritative compiler (cargo check --all-targets) actually compiled clean.
open_items: Wave 7 (plan 13, desktop-e2e real-mount acceptance leg, autonomous:false) still pending — requires human sign-off checkpoint, dispatch-gated CI round-trip.
WinFsp parity gap: crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs still carries the old (pre-D-15d) gate-ordering pattern; cannot be verified on macOS, flagged as a follow-up.
